# Green-Bond Architecture for Multi-Jurisdiction Decarbonization Capex
## EU / North Africa / Southeast Asia — Issuance Program 2026–2028

*Parameter note: EU Green Bond Standard application, CSRD/Omnibus scope, ASEAN Taxonomy versioning, Singapore-Asia Taxonomy transition sunsets, and Gulf national taxonomies are all in active flux. This design treats criteria as **versioned inputs**, not fixed constraints — the governance layer is built to absorb drift without re-opening issued documentation.*

---

## 1. Framing: the real problem is not taxonomy divergence

Three problems are being conflated, and they need different solutions:

| Apparent problem | Actual problem | Solution layer |
|---|---|---|
| "Taxonomies conflict" | Eligibility perimeters differ, but **assets don't move** — one asset can hold different labels in different markets | Asset tiering + instrument matching |
| "Disclosure standards differ" | ESRS, ISSB S2, ASEAN GBS, AAOIFI are largely **nested, not contradictory** | Single measurement spine, layered reporting |
| "Advisers conflict" | Rating agencies, SPO providers and banks have **different commercial books** — consensus is not available and not the goal | Group becomes the standard-setter; publish the deltas |
| "Plant data is inconsistent" | This is the **binding constraint**. It caps issuance size, instrument choice, and credibility | Data-maturity gating (Section 4) |

**Core thesis:** do not build one instrument that satisfies every taxonomy. That produces a lowest-common-denominator eligible pool, shrinks issuance capacity, and still fails somewhere. Build **one asset register and one measurement spine, wrapped in market-specific instruments.**

---

## 2. Rejected alternatives (and why)

- **Single global green bond at the intersection of all taxonomies.** Eligible pool collapses to ~30–40% of retrofit capex; North Africa and SEA assets are effectively excluded from financing precisely where capital is scarcest. Rejected.
- **Three independent frameworks, one per region.** Guarantees inconsistent claims about the same assets across jurisdictions — the single largest greenwashing-litigation exposure. Rejected.
- **Lead with a sustainability-linked bond (SLB) to sidestep asset eligibility.** Counterintuitive but wrong: SLBs require *higher* data quality than use-of-proceeds bonds, because the KPI is an audited, restatement-proof entity-level time series. With Grade-C plants in the perimeter, an SLB is a credibility landmine. **Defer SLBs to Phase 3.**
- **Wait for taxonomy convergence.** Convergence is a decade away; retrofit capex is now. Rejected.

---

## 3. Asset architecture: the three-tier ledger

Every retrofit project enters a single group register and receives one tier assignment. Tiers can be downgraded, never double-counted, and are auditable.

| Tier | Definition | Typical assets | Fundable by |
|---|---|---|---|
| **T1 — Universal Green** | Meets EU Taxonomy TSC + DNSH + minimum safeguards, and by construction meets ASEAN/Gulf/ICMA criteria | Waste-heat recovery, motor/drive & compressed-air upgrades, on-site solar + storage, electrification of process heat under renewable PPA, green H₂, water/circularity | EuGB-labelled bond, any instrument |
| **T2 — Regional Green / Transition** | Eligible under ASEAN Taxonomy (amber), Singapore-Asia transition category, Gulf frameworks, or Japanese transition guidance — but fails EU TSC or lacks DNSH evidence | Coal-to-gas CHP switch, grid electrification in coal-heavy grids, efficiency gains below EU thresholds, bridging fuels in North Africa | Green sukuk, ASEAN transition bond, local-currency bank facilities, DFI blended structures |
| **T3 — Not-yet-eligible** | Fails all criteria **or** sits at a plant with Grade-C measurement | Anything at a data-deficient site; ambiguous-technology capex | Conventional debt, ECA facilities, RCF — **no label, no claim** |

The tier boundary is deliberately drawn by the *strictest binding criterion*, not the most convenient one. T2 assets are financed honestly as transition, not laundered into a green label.

**Exploit the EuGB 15% flexibility pocket deliberately.** The EU Green Bond Standard permits up to 15% of proceeds for activities in sectors without technical screening criteria. Reserve this pocket for North Africa / SEA assets in criteria-less sectors — it is the legitimate bridge that most issuers waste on domestic assets.

run.userPrompt:
In 2026, an industrial group with plants in Europe, North Africa, and Southeast Asia wants to finance decarbonization retrofits through green bonds. Taxonomy definitions, disclosure standards, and investor ESG expectations differ across the EU, Gulf, and Asian capital markets, and internal plants report emissions with inconsistent measurement quality. Rating agencies and regional banks give conflicting guidance.

Propose a financing strategy that structures green-bond issuance across markets with divergent taxonomies and disclosure standards, while managing measurement-quality risk and protecting the group's credibility with investors.
